name: INDONESIA
lead: Indonesia is the world's biggest archipelago — over 17,000 islands wider than the USA. Volcanoes rumble under rainforests where orangutans swing through the canopy. Ancient temples rise from rice terraces, and the seas burst with so much colour that snorkellers barely need to search for fish — they are simply everywhere.
geo: Indonesia sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire with 130 active volcanoes — more than any other country. Krakatoa's 1883 eruption was heard in Australia, 3,100 km away.
The archipelago stretches 5,100 km east to west — roughly London to Tehran. Islands range from jungle mountains to flat coral atolls barely above the waves.
animals: Sumatra is the only place where tigers, elephants, rhinos, and orangutans all share one rainforest. The Komodo dragon — up to 3 m long — lives only on a handful of Indonesian islands.
The Coral Triangle around eastern Indonesia holds the richest marine life on Earth: 600+ coral species and 3,000 kinds of fish, from whale sharks to pygmy seahorses.
culture: Indonesia has 300+ ethnic groups and 700 languages, yet Bahasa Indonesia unites them all at school. Wayang kulit shadow puppet shows, lasting all night, are on UNESCO's heritage list.
Batik cloth — wax-resist dyed in intricate patterns — is worn at weddings and offices alike. The gamelan orchestra's bronze gongs create shimmering music like a waterfall of notes.
history: Hindu and Buddhist kingdoms thrived here for a thousand years; Borobudur (c. 800 CE) is the world's largest Buddhist monument. Later, Muslim sultanates commanded the global spice trade.
The Dutch ruled for three and a half centuries, drawn by nutmeg, pepper, and cloves. Sukarno declared independence on 17 August 1945 — a date every Indonesian knows by heart.
wows: Indonesia has more active volcanoes than any other country — about 130.
Java holds 155 million people, making it the most densely populated large island on Earth.
Komodo dragons can detect prey with their tongue from up to 9 km away.
Borobudur's 2,672 relief panels, laid end to end, would stretch over 6 km.
Indonesia grows around 75% of the world's nutmeg — more than any other nation.
The motto 'Bhinneka Tunggal Ika' — Unity in Diversity — was written 700 years ago.
Indonesia is relocating its capital to a brand-new jungle city called Nusantara in Borneo.

myths.fact: Bali is one of 17,000+ islands. Most Indonesians are Muslim — Bali's Hindu culture is a beautiful, rare exception, not the national norm.
Papua's Puncak Jaya (4,884 m) carries a glacier — one of the last tropical glaciers outside the Andes, and scientists warn it may vanish by 2030.
